tag: Earnings season meets the Fed calendar
title: Do earnings get read differently when the Fed is talking?
sub: 421,885 US earnings releases since 2005, timed to the second. Pre-registered, holdout run once. Short answer: I can't find it.
meta_r: code and data in the first comment

tag: Q1 · How crowded is the calendar?
a_l: earnings 8-Ks on an FOMC statement day
sub: The Fed meets eight times a year, always inside reporting season. One release in seven first trades in the same session as CPI, the jobs report or the FOMC statement.

tag: Q1 · How crowded is the calendar? · orange dots are FOMC days
title: Every quarter the FOMC lands in the thick of reporting season
Pre-market or after the close? EDGAR's timestamp tells me, to the second.
sub: A 06:46 filing on a CPI day competes with the 08:30 print. A 16:30 filing on Fed day competes with nothing until the next open.

title: How the test was built
steps: Every 8-K with Item 2.02 from EDGAR; time of day from the acceptance stamp.
Crowded: the news first trades in the same session as CPI, payrolls or the FOMC statement.
Surprise two ways: first-filed GAAP EPS against last year, and the two-day market move.
Drift over 60 days against FF5 plus momentum; firm and quarter fixed effects; errors clustered by firm and day.
Thresholds written down first. 2016–2025 held out and run once.

tag: Q2 · Does crowding change the drift? · baseline
title: Post-earnings drift is still alive: 1 to 4 pp a year, except 2020
sub: 60-day drift, top vs bottom surprise decile, with 95% bands. If nothing drifts, there's nothing for Fed day to change.

tag: Q2 · Does crowding change the drift?
title: Crowded releases drift 1.1 pp, quiet ones 1.5 pp. The gap is inside the noise.
sub: Top minus bottom surprise decile after the two-day reaction. 26,531 extreme events, 2005–2025.

title: First sample: −1.5 pp, all on FOMC days. Holdout: +0.75 pp, nothing. It doesn't replicate.
sub: Blue: the primary test in each sample. Grey: by release type. Extra 60-day drift, top vs bottom decile, on crowded sessions.

title: 1,000 random macro calendars: 30% produce a bigger coefficient than the real one
sub: If the real calendar mattered, it should sit in the tail. It sits in the middle.

tag: Q2 · positive control · exploratory, not pre-registered
title: Illiquid names drift 3.6x more, so the drift is real. Crowding still adds nothing.
sub: Split by bid-ask spread (Corwin-Schultz estimate). The crowded-session effect is flat in all three groups.

tag: Q3 · Do firms time bad news to the Fed?
title: No. Weak quarters land on crowded sessions at the same rate as good ones.
sub: Share with EPS below last year, both samples. Regression t-stats −0.01 and 1.2.

title: What weak quarters do shift is the filing: more late 8-Ks, more Friday nights
sub: 1 pp more likely to file after the release day, within firm, t 5.8 on 177,209 announcements. Friday after close 1.7% vs 1.4%.

tag: Q4 · Can you trade it? · exploratory
title: No. Neither book covers its spread costs.
sub: Quiet-session events: 1.2 bp a day, t 1.9, 237 names. Crowded: 0.6 bp, t 0.4, 50 names. After bid-ask costs both lose.

title: What I'd challenge if this were someone else's work
items: Prices come from Yahoo Finance, so most delisted firms are missing. Their crowded share was 14.6% against 15.9% for survivors.
GAAP EPS against last year isn't the consensus number analysts actually trade.
The holdout standard error is 0.66 pp: an effect under about 1.3 pp, top versus bottom decile, could still be there.
Slides marked exploratory weren't pre-registered. 737 tickers that moved more than 100% in a day were dropped whole.

title: My read: the market prices earnings about as fully on Fed day as on any other.
sub: Firms don't use crowded sessions to bury weak quarters; what they delay is the 8-K itself. What would change my mind: a consensus-based surprise, or prices for the delisted firms, showing a gap this data can't see.
